title: Humidity Control Beyond the AC
desc: HVAC experts explain the importance of humidity control in San Antonio and how to tell if your home needs a dehumidifier.

blocks.text: Having a comfortable home is essential when the temperature outside becomes unbearable. Extreme heat leads to fatigue, headaches, dehydration, and heat stroke. Maintaining your home’s comfort reduces these risks. It also helps you sleep better, which adds to better mental health. Furthermore, a hot home makes your body work harder. This causes strain on the heart and respiratory system. These issues affect children, the elderly, and pets the most. While an efficient and effective cooling system helps, you also need to consider the humidity levels in your home. If the AC isn’t enough, a whole-home dehumidifier is essential. The two will work together to ensure your comfort, even during the hottest seasons.
How a Whole-Home Dehumidifier Works

A whole-home dehumidifier integrates with your existing HVAC system. It pulls excess moisture from the air inside your house. While a portable dehumidifier will handle a single room, whole-home options treat the air throughout your home by connecting directly to your ductwork.

A whole-home dehumidifier has a humidity sensor. This humidistat monitors your indoor moisture levels. Once the humidity rises above a set level, the humidistat triggers the system. The system pulls air in from the return ductwork and into the dehumidifier. This air then passes over refrigerant-filled evaporator coils. As the warm, moist air cools, the water vapor condenses and forms liquid droplets on the coils. These droplets drip into a pan or reservoir. From there, it escapes through a designated drain line. Since whole-home dehumidifiers connect to your plumbing system, there’s no need to manually empty this water. The now drier air flows back into your supply ducts. These ducts redistribute this air throughout your home.
Typical Installation Methods

Return-to-supply installations pull air from your main return duct and force the dry air into the supply plenum. This method allows the air to bypass your AC’s wet evaporator coil, which increases efficiency.
Return-to-return installations draw from the exhaust back into your main return duct. This is less efficient due to how the dry air might pick up moisture from the AC’s wet coils.

With a dedicated return installation, the dehumidifier will use its own air intake vents. These are separate from your HVAC system’s return. These systems draw air from specific areas with humidity issues, such as a basement.
Why Dry Air Feels Cooler

Understanding why dry air feels cooler than cold air during humid Texas springs helps you understand the importance of dehumidifiers. In general, dry air allows your body to regulate its temperature more easily.

When humidity levels are lower, the air has more room to absorb water vapor. This leads to your sweat evaporating more quickly. When your body can remove heat faster, you’ll feel cooler, even when the temperature remains the same. This is why you’ll feel cooler on a dry, 70°F day than on a rainy, humid 70°F day.

When humidity levels are high, there’s excessive moisture in the air. This keeps your sweat from evaporating efficiently. Instead, it stays on your skin, which makes you feel hot and sticky. Since this is trapping your heat, your core temperature can rise. This leads to an uncomfortable, overheated feeling.
The Key Benefits of a Whole-Home Dehumidifier

A whole-home dehumidifier helps you keep your indoor humidity levels within an ideal range. This is typically between 40% and 60%. As a result, they help prevent bacteria, mold, and mildew growth that can cause respiratory problems and allergic reactions. Some molds produce mycotoxins, which lead to headaches, fatigue, and serious health issues. Dehumidifiers also help reduce dust mites and other allergens. This provides symptom relief for those suffering from allergies or asthma.

Whole-home dehumidifiers enhance your comfort. High indoor humidity levels leave you feeling warm and sticky. Removing the excess moisture from the air helps you feel comfortable, even at higher temperatures. This can allow you to set your AC thermostat a little higher, which may save energy and system wear and tear.

A dehumidifier can help protect your property. High humidity levels lead to moisture-related problems, such as warping wood floors, structural wood rot, and peeling paint. Lower humidity also helps you avoid corrosion on your electronics.

Whole-home dehumidifiers are a low-maintenance option. Single room, portable dehumidifiers require you to routinely empty the drain pan. Whole-home systems connect to your plumbing system, which eliminates this job. These systems usually require an annual cleaning of the filter.
What to Expect During Installation

The installation process begins with choosing the right whole-home dehumidifier for your needs. A technician will calculate your capacity needs according to your square footage and humidity levels. A very damp home will require a higher-capacity system. By using specialized tools, such as a hydrometer, they can get a precise baseline. This is more accurate than relying on subjective feelings. If you have a basement or crawlspace, they’ll include these areas in their calculations.

When it’s time to install the whole-home dehumidifier, your installer will find a central location for it. This is near your HVAC system. They may need to install a hanging kit or platform to help support the system and prevent vibrations. The technician will also need to cut into your supply and return plenum to connect the system. Back dampers will prevent air from flowing backward into the device when it’s off. Because these systems drain automatically, your installer will run a PVC line to your floor drain. If necessary, they’ll include a condensate pump to push the water uphill.

When it comes to electronics and controls, most whole-home dehumidifiers require a dedicated 120V circuit. The technician will also mount the humidistat in a central living area. This allows you to easily reach it and set your desired humidity level.

Once they complete the installation, you should notice immediate comfort. The air will feel lighter and less sticky within three to six hours. By 12 to 24 hours, you’ll notice the full impact. This is enough time for the dehumidifier to stabilize humidity levels throughout the house.
